newsitem.title: JAPAN: Toyota says may develop European compact car.
newsitem.headline: Toyota says may develop European compact car.

text.p: Toyota Motor Corp is considering developing a compact car designed exclusively for the European market that would be smaller than any of the firm's existing models, a company spokesman said on Friday.
But the spokesman said the company had not yet decided where the special European compact car would be manufactured if Toyota, Japan's biggest carmaker, decided to go ahead with the plan.

Toyota president Hiroshi Okuda was quoted by the Asian Wall Street Journal on Thursday as saying in an interview that Toyota was planning to launch a European compact car to be built somewhere in Europe after the turn of the century.

The Toyota spokesman, quoting Okuda, confirmed that Toyota is considering developing a car "tailored to preferences in Europe" but added there was no decision on when the model might be launched and where it would be manufactured.

It was not clear what particular design features the company had in mind to cater to European tastes. However, the spokesman said the idea was to produce something smaller than the Starlet, the smallest car in the current Toyota line-up.
The Asian Wall Street Journal report quoted analysts as saying that the new model could be a microcar that would rival Fiat's Cinquecento models and Ford's Ka.

The production site for the new model would be closely watched for clues to Toyota's European strategy after a controversy earlier this year over the future of its investment in Britain after the launch of a single European currency.

Earlier this month, Britain's Financial Times reported that Toyota plans to build a $1.6 billion car plant in northern France as its second plant in Europe. The company said at the time, however, that it was still studying many possible options for its European investment.
Toyota currently has a car plant in Britain which produced 117,000 cars in calender 1996.
The company said previously that it aims to sell 600,000 cars annually in Europe after the turn of the century, compared with a target of 450,000 car sales in Europe in 1997.
Okuda stirred a controversy in February when he said Toyota would rather put new investment in continental Europe than Britain if Britain stayed outside Europe's single currency.
